items.title: Elden Ring Leak: 4 Unseen NPCs and Cut Dialogue [2026]
'Elden Ring' Creators' Next Fantasy Game Officially Delayed to 2027
items.summary: The Duskbloods, the next game from the creators of Elden Ring and Bloodborne, has been officially delayed to 2027. Read on for more.
items.content:
elden ring Image via FromSoftware Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Adam Blevins Published Oct 29, 2026, 1:28 PM EDT Adam Blevins began working in the entertainment industry in 2022 as a Staff Writer for Agents of Fandom, where he progressed to Senior Editor and interviewed talent from Marvel Studios , House of the Dragon , and Planet of the Apes . He joined Collider as a News Author in April 2024, was promoted to a Senior position in December 2024, and has written over 3,000 articles for the site, including exclusives relating to Avengers: Doomsday , The Penguin , Star Wars: Skeleton Crew , and more. He primarily writes about the latest box office numbers and the hottest movies and TV shows on streaming, while also covering superhero and sci-fi news. He has completed a set visit for The Chosen and even has several months of experience writing Gaming Features at ScreenRant . You can find him on X , LinkedIn , and Muckrack . Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There have been plenty of great games released in the last few years, but not many have had the same cultural impact as Elden Ring , which is still one of the most-played games on Steam and other platforms years later. The game was developed by FromSoftware, the same studio behind the Bloodborne and Dark Souls games, and it was co-written by George R.R. Martin , the legendary author whose writings inspired Game of Thrones . Elden Ring is even being turned into a movie courtesy of writer/director Alex Garland , and it’s confirmed to be A24’s most expensive movie ever , boasting a budget of nearly $200 million. The movie has already wrapped filming, but it isn’t coming to theaters until 2028, which leaves the post-production team with plenty of time to make the final polishes before it comes out.

Next up on the slate for FromSoftware is The DuskBloods , which is being developed in collaboration with Nintendo as a Switch 2 exclusive — this means that the game will not launch on XBOX, PlayStation , or PC. Since the game was announced in 2024, it was thought that The Duskbloods would be released before the end of 2026, but this is no longer the case. FromSoftware announced in a new press release this afternoon that The Duskbloods has officially been delayed to 2027 to give the development team more time to focus on combat, strategic depth, and player expression. There was growing concern that the game would be delayed when it was completely left out of the September 2026 Nintendo Direct show, which came after the game experienced server issues that prevented players from logging in.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Alex Garland wrote the script and directed the Elden Ring movie by himself, but George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki are credited as writers on the project as well for their work crafting the story for the video game. A24 has loaded up a star-studded cast for the Elden Ring movie as well, with Jonathan Pryce , Cailee Spaeny , Tom Burke , Nick Offerman , Havana Rose Liu , Sonoya Mizuno , Kit Connor , Ben Whishaw , Jefferson Hall , and more all being tapped for key roles in the film. Casting details are being kept under wraps, but the movie is being described as faithful to the game and full of epic cinematic moments.

Stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of The Duskbloods and the Elden Ring movie coming to theaters in 2028.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero has the perfect solution to Elden Ring's biggest buzzkill
items.summary: Opinion | This new action RPG solves one of my biggest problems with Soulslikes
items.content:
Opinion | This new action RPG solves one of my biggest problems with Soulslikes

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: S-Game) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Phantom Blade Zero is the best action RPG I've played all year. The staggering variety of imaginative weapons available to wuxia hero Soul, all painstakingly animated via authentic martial arts choreography, is what really sets the game apart. This is not a Soulslike. You lose nothing upon death, enemies never respawn, stamina is plentiful, there are no RPG stats, and you will restart at phase two of a boss if you clear phase one. Yet Phantom Blade Zero solves two of my biggest complaints with most Soulslikes, one of which still bothers me whenever I sit down to play Elden Ring on a new character.

Nothing bums me out faster than barely surviving a tough boss fight and then eagerly sprinting to the blacksmith to forge their weapon, only to learn it has almost the exact same move set as the longsword I found in a bin 40 hours ago. This instrument of death feared across the lands is, actually, a normal sword with better stats. If I'm lucky, it may have a special charged attack – often one so slow that I can only use it against most enemies by giving 14 days advance notice.

Weapons in Phantom Blade Zero – the main ones that you swing all the time, and the sub-weapons you break out for special occasions – all feel distinct, and almost every major boss drops one (there are a lot of bosses). There are a lot of swords in this game too, and it feels great to swing them, to hear steel clash like colliding icebergs. There are also twinned daggers that attack on their own, gauntlets that pulverize the very air, great swords that trade your health for damage, chained axes that would be the envy of Kratos, and literal instruments whose plucked strings send searing arcs of energy tearing through enemies. Swords extend, spirits surround you, bludgeons spin like food processors (dude processors, if you will), and fire roars at your request.

Now for the best part. You're perfectly capable of using all of these weapons all the time . Elden Ring is full of unique dispensers of death, but its weapon upgrade system is so laborious that you're often stuck with a handful of weapons until you get very late in the game and materials become buyable. Even then, you can only max out a few weapons each playthrough. The question is not, "Do I like this new sword more?" Instead, you wonder, "Can I upgrade this to the same level as ol' reliable?" Don't take me to a buffet and then give me a plate the size of my fist. I wanna pig out! I wanna try it all, and Phantom Blade Zero lets me.

When you upgrade a weapon in Phantom Blade Zero, you dump materials into it to boost its attack power and unlock additional bonuses and attacks. One-handed, two-handed, and dual-wielded weapons have their own upgrade materials, as do different archetypes of sub-weapons. This encourages you to use, say, a one-handed sword and a dual weapon so that you can upgrade them both maximally, whereas two different one-handed swords would compete for materials.

After 3 hours, Phantom Blade Zero is a wuxia-flavored, rewarding action-RPG with a fresh Soulslike twist Phantom Blade Zero's Metacritic score lands it as one of the top action games of 2026 Phantom Blade Zero review: "A GOTY contender with combat that looks as good as it feels" If you ever want to change weapons, you can just downgrade your current one to refund all the stones and XP that went into it. It's so easy. It doesn't cost anything until you hit level 10, and even then it only requires a coupon I've found dozens of. It's such a simple and elegant system. Finding upgrade materials doesn't enhance one weapon – it increases the effective level of all your weapons.

It's hard to overstate how much this one change improves the flow of a playthrough. Every new boss weapon is exciting because I know I can immediately use it. There are no stats or stones to hold me back. I change weapons all the time in Phantom Blade Zero – not because I get bored, but because I want everything.

The best games of 2026 so far, with plenty still to come.

Austin Wood Social Links Navigation Senior writer Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible.

items.title: Switch 2 Exclusive The Duskbloods Officially Delayed, Now Set for 2027
items.summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive is steering clear of GTA 6
items.content:
By Michael McWhertor Published Oct 29, 2026, 10:12 AM EDT Michael McWhertor is a New York-based journalist and editor with more than 20 years of experience covering games, industry events, technology, movies, and TV. News FromSoftware's new PvPvE game won't arrive on Switch 2 this year as planned

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover The Duskbloods Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap FromSoftware's The Duskbloods won't make its previously announced 2026 release window. The Elden Ring and Bloodborne developer announced Thursday that its Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive will now be released sometime in 2027. FromSoftware said in a statement that it's working to adjust the game's "rules and balance" following a player test this summer.

Fans had already started to suspect The Duskbloods wouldn't squeeze into the remaining weeks of the year, especially since it would be competing with Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 , which is launching in November.

Here's FromSoftware's full official statement:

During the network test in August 2026, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including direct combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects of the game and improve the player experience, we have made the decision to move the release window, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

We offer our sincere apologies to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title. Your understanding and patience are greatly appreciated.

The studio posted a slightly different message directly to its followers on X :

Regarding the software "The Duskbloods" for the Nintendo Switch 2, we have decided to allocate a period for final adjustments to the game rules and balance. This is in order to realize the concept of this title—enjoyable not only through direct combat but also through various maneuvers and diverse strategies—at an even higher level, based on the evaluations received from all users during the network test held in August, and to deliver an even better gaming experience. As a result, we will be changing the release date to 2027. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this will cause to those of you who have been eagerly awaiting the game, and we kindly ask for your understanding.

The Duskbloods is a new type of multiplayer experience for FromSoftware, with an emphasis on PvPvE mechanics. The game gives players control of characters called Bloodsworn, who fight monsters and other Bloodsworn players in online multiplayer matches in a battle for survival. Unlike Dark Souls and Elden Ring , The Duskbloods focuses less on players charging forward against challenging odds, dying repeatedly, and charging forward again. It is instead a match-based multiplayer game in which eight players fight to earn victory points called Virtue, with multiple possible pathways to victory.

The Duskbloods will be FromSoftware's first new game since last year's Elden Ring Nightreign . Game director Hidetaka Miyazaki says he hopes The Duskbloods ' game design leads to "unexpected drama." The studio recently held a limited network test for the game, offering FromSoftware fans a peek at its characters and mechanics.

The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive is an odd but compelling mix of gameplay styles

items.title: Elden Ring Movie Could Be Over 3 Hours Long
items.summary: The Elden Ring Movie is building steam, and it's been revealed that the screenplay is reportedly 180 pages and could run 3 hours.
items.content:
One of the biggest headaches with the Elden Ring Movie will always be: ‘How do you capture the magic and essence of a game that, to see and do everything, can take you upwards of 100 hours?’

It’s a dilemma, and even if the Elden Ring Movie was split into multiple films, plenty of stuff will be missed. This is before you even consider the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. According to Deadline, the script for Elden Ring is finished, and the movie could be very long.

From the humble beginnings in The Lands Between to the final fight against the Elden Beast, a lot happens. The Elden Ring Movie won’t include every single boss fight in epic detail, as that would require multiple episodes of weekly TV—which this project might have been better suited to.

Regardless, Deadline reports that ‘In what seems to be an industry first, A24 is flying members of its team directly to international buyers for them to read the script with the staffer present.’

‘It’s a long read; we hear it runs to at least 180 pages with visuals, implying the movie could push towards three hours.’

Classic filmmaking suggests one page of a screenplay equates to one minute—give or take a few seconds. It varies depending on how much dialogue is on the page, if it’s a detailed and lengthy establishing shot, or something else that needs time to digest. Also, ‘at least’ is a minimum, meaning we could go well over three hours!

A24 appears to be going all in on the movie, highlighted by A24’s Elden Ring Movie apparently costing nearly $200 million —making it easily the company’s most expensive production ever.

A big budget and a lengthy script could be a recipe for the most epic fantasy film, and it’s more than likely you will witness true horror.

Is 3 hours overkill? Or is this not enough to tell the full story? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming Discord server .

For more Insider Gaming content, check out ‘ GTA 6 Won’t Let You Speedrun the Main Story ,’ and don’t forget to sign up for our newsletter .

items.title: Roblox developers use AI to port exact replicas of Elden Ring, Counter-Strike, Sonic Generations
items.summary: Many of these ports have since been taken down.
items.content:
All News AI-assisted Roblox games featured exact replicas of Elden Ring, CS, and more (Image: Bandai Namco).

{" "} Roblox developers use AI to port exact replicas of Elden Ring, Counter-Strike, Sonic Generations .iframe-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .img-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .a-img-media {aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} Many of these ports have since been taken down. Roblox has long struggled with users recreating existing games on its platform, but the rise of AI technology is taking the problem to a whole new level.

A new wave of reportedly AI-assisted game ports has emerged on Roblox, featuring blatant copies of existing video games with ripped assets and identical user interfaces. Titles from publishers such as Valve , Bandai Namco , and SEGA are among those recreated on the platform.

While some of these ports have been taken down, whether following warnings, through action by the platform itself or at the creators' discretion, several games that plagiarise the originals remain available.

One of the earliest sightings of these Roblox AI ports was a recreation of the entire PlayStation console experience. In a clip shared by content creator KreekCraft , we see a replica of the console's user interface, complete with its boot screen and several playable games.

The games featured on the home screen include Five Nights at Freddy's, Undertale, The Simpsons: Hit & Run, Clustertruck, SUPERHOT, Gang Beasts, and PaRappa the Rapper. More recently, the Xbox 360 has also been recreated on Roblox, featuring the same line-up of games.

Several Valve titles have also been copied onto the platform, including very identical recreations of Counter-Strike, Halo , and Left 4 Dead 2 .

One particularly viral post showed a recreation of Elden Ring in Roblox. The level of detail is astonishing, with the game featuring the similar audio, environments, cutscenes and combat, all rendered in Roblox's art style. It is even said to feature working multiplayer.

Although many of these ports have since been removed, we have found several more examples that closely replicate licensed intellectual property.

One is SEGA's Sonic Generations Multiplayer , based on the 2011 platformer Sonic Generations. Having tried it ourselves, we found that it is an exact copy of the original game, although it appears to feature only the Green Hill Classic map.

X user Sunny , who claims to have ported Sonic Generations to Roblox, said they used “AI-assisted tools” while manually debugging the game and “making sure the game works as intended”. The game has attracted relatively few players, recording more than 8,000 visits since launching on 24 October. However, Sunny's other port, which recreates Five Nights at Freddy's, has amassed more than 4.7 million visits.

Roblox's open platform gives users the freedom to create their own games. As a result, many have attempted to recreate popular titles, offering an easy way to attract traffic and potentially generate revenue.

When Meccha Chameleon took off in the friendslop space, countless copies of the game appeared on Roblox. One recreation, Chameleon!, has amassed 94 million visits, while Paint and Seek! has collected more than 213 million. Another inspired title, Paint or Die! has recorded 185 million visits.

The same pattern has emerged with other simple, viral games, including the fashion game Dressmaker , Among Us, and Needle in a Haystack. The developer of the latter even recently shared a satirical “find the original game” post , shading the many clones of their viral hit.

items.title: 5 Greatest Open-World Games of the Last 5 Years, Ranked
items.summary: Some of the greatest open-world games of all time, like Elden Ring, were released in the last 5 years.
items.content:
The Tarnished in Elden Ring Image via FromSoftware Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Mark O’Callaghan Published Oct 28, 2026, 7:30 PM EDT Mark is the lead gaming critic for CBR who passionately shares his reviews of the latest video games. He's been hooked on gaming since getting a Nintendo GameCube and Super Mario Sunshine. It took him a while to decide what he wanted to do, but soon, he realized that talking about pop culture and gaming could be a career. After graduating from the College of Saint Rose, he's been writing since and sharing his passion for those inclined to read. When Mark is not writing, he's playing games, reading comics, watching the latest TV show, and hanging out with his dog, Kara (named after Supergirl). He also hosted the KeenGamer podcast at one point and has appeared on other pop culture podcasts like The Brazilian Dragon. With his reviews, Mark conveys whether you should buy the game or not with concise points and analysis. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Advancements in technology have made open-world games bigger and better, and some of the best games in the entire genre were released in the last five years. While titles like Skyrim and Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild raised the bar for open-world games, newer games have built on the foundation they've laid.

Many open-world games have been released in the 2020s, but there are a handful of titles that rank far above the rest. These games showcase the potential of the open-world genre, and because they contain massive and beautifully crafted worlds, they can keep players busy for dozens of hours.

Horizon Forbidden West protagonist Aloy swims Image via Guerrilla Games Horizon Forbidden West is one of the best-looking games of this generation and has one of the most stunning open-worlds of all time . Every detail in the game, whether it's the gorgeous color palette or little details like the foliage, comes together to create a visual treat. 4 years after its release, no game has come close to its visuals.

Not only does Horizon Forbidden West look incredible, but it's fantastic to play as well. The world is a joy to explore, and hunting adds another layer of excitement. Players have to plan out each encounter against the game's massive machines, and that makes victories all the more satisfying.

Since it's a direct sequel to Horizon Zero Dawn , it's not necessarily the best entry point to the series, and newcomers may not understand some aspects of its story. That said, Horizon Zero West is worth the effort. Both games in the franchise are examples of why people love open-world games so much.

Miles and Peter in Marvel's Spider-Man 2 Image via Insomniac The sequel to Marvel’s Spider-Man was one of the most anticipated PlayStation 5 games, and it absolutely delivered. Playing as both Peter and Miles feels meaningfully different without either character overshadowing the other. Thanks to the power of the PS5, loading times are essentially nonexistent in Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 , making character switching feel completely seamless.

Fast travel is quicker than ever, but it’s almost unnecessary when swinging through New York City feels this good. The already excellent web-slinging has been refined even further, and the addition of web wings adds a real sense of speed and momentum to traversal. These mechanics pair perfectly with new abilities, including the symbiote powers, which add extra flair to combat.

Taking down thugs and working through the trophy list is consistently rewarding, resulting in a platinum run that’s satisfying without dragging on. For anyone who wants to truly feel like Spider-Man, Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 more than delivers on that fantasy. Even people who aren't Spider-Man fans will get swept away by this incredible game.

Image via Warhorse Studios At first, playing Kingdom Come: Deliverance II mirrors Henry’s own experience. Players begin poor, dirty, and struggling in Bohemia, with the world feeling actively stacked against them. Over time, though, everything starts to click, and exploration becomes genuinely rewarding. The game gives players just enough direction to make wandering the world feel purposeful rather than overwhelming.

Players might stumble across a single event that spirals into a layered side quest just as compelling as the main story. The game constantly encourages engagement, as progression is tied directly to what players do. The more players focus on a specific skill, like one-handed combat, the more that skill improves.

items.title: The Road to A24’s ‘Elden Ring’ Movie Runs Longer Than Anyone Expected
Review – The Relic: First Guardian
items.summary: More like the smel-lic, am I right?
items.content:
Action RPGs are actually one of my favourite genres of game, but finding the good ones is more difficult than it should be sometimes. You’ve got games like Diablo , Elden Ring , Mass Effect , and The Witcher to compete with. So having the chance to check out a new one, The Relic: First Guardian , I couldn’t say no, simply because I would love something that is gonna grab my attention for a longer playthrough like this genre tends to offer.

The Relic: First Guardian , takes place in a world destroyed by the Great Relic. You’re, as the name suggests, the guardian of the relic, but you have amnesia and can’t remember what your goal is. Not very convenient, isn’t it? You follow a mysterious voice around the world, collect shards of the relic, seek to honor the voices of those who came before you, save the world, happy days.

Somebody call 911! Shawty fire burning on the dance floor!

The biggest difference from the majority of ARPGs is the fact there’s no traditional levelling system. There’s no XP granted from defeating enemies, besides money. There’s actually no point to defeating enemies as it stands in this current system. Now, money can be looked at the same way as Souls/Ruins in a way. Gold is used to buy weapon, health, and stamina upgrades, so it’s a semi-familiar feeling to Soulslike fans.

One key difference in this respect is none of it is lost if you die, which means no corpse runs to make sure you don’t lose anything. Realistically, there’s actually no negative to dying, it’s just more of an inconvenience. Although, if you look around for the runestones where you save your progress (basically this game’s bonfires), there are plenty around so you’re never far from the action. This further takes away an semblance of challenge.

I found another site of gra… Wait, wrong game.

The Relic: First Guardian keeps most situations to one on one combat. There aren’t a lot of spots, unless you choose to run through everything, where multiple enemies will attack you at the same time. There’s essentially two types of enemies, if you really want to dumb it down. The ones that get staggered and the ones that don’t. The enemies that get staggered are obviously incredibly easy, you hit them and they don’t swing back. Obviously, the types that don’t take a bit more effort because the recovery time after each attack is fairly unforgiving. Unlike a game like Dark Souls , you can’t seem to dodge through attacks, so you need to aim to dodge out of range.

You also have an ability you can use to help damage enemies, starting with a fireball. I found this to be incredibly frustrating because half the time I pressed L and R to use it, it didn’t seem to want to activate, it was just making me aim in the middle of fighting an enemy or a boss and throwing me off. On that note, I know after Elden Ring , saying this game has 80+ bosses is nothing, but between the rather unforgiving recovery time, and what feels like no I-frames, even the simplest boss can be a little frustrating.

So what’s the verdict? The Relic: First Guardian has some systems that are clearly borrowed from other ARPG games, but simply not incorporated very well. It wants to play like a Soulslike, but doesn’t have the fluidity. It wants to have weapon specific gear builds, but everything is based around the weapon skill trees and not finding upgraded gear. There’s next to no reason to refight enemies, and outside of a little frustration there’s no penalty to dying so you may as well just run through areas. End of the day, there are a lot of games that do every mechanic The Relic: First Guardian does, but better, so it’s not exactly worth the time investment.

Far from the best looking game available on Switch 2. It’s not the worst looking game you could play, but I can’t think of many that offer less visually Gameplay: 4.0

Wants to be baby’s first Soulslike. Wants to be baby’s first ARPG. Misses the mark on everything it’s aiming to be, which just creates a mess of gameplay mechanics. Sound: 2.5

There’s almost nothing to say here. The voice acting doesn’t sound genuine, the ambient sound doesn’t make the world feel alive. Fun Factor: 3.0

There haven’t been a lot of games this year I’m actively going to avoid playing more. This is one of them though. Final Verdict: 3.5 The Relic: First Guardian is available now on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S.

A copy of The Relic: First Guardian was provided by the publisher .

items.title: Elden Ring Movie Runtime Could Push Three Hours, Script Hints
items.summary: A few new details on the story for A24’s Elden Ring movie have emerged, including its possible runtime. And, if that remains the case, it’s going to be epic.
items.content:
A few new details on the story for A24’s Elden Ring movie have emerged, including its possible runtime. And, if that remains the case, it’s going to be epic.

Deadline reports that writer-director Alex Garland’s screenplay , based on FromSoftware’s acclaimed fantasy video game, “runs to at least 180 pages with visuals, implying the movie could push towards three hours. While plot details are largely being kept under wraps, we understand that in-demand Heartstopper actor [Kit] Connor is the protagonist and the ‘faithful’ film will follow his journey. There are said to be battles between his character and impressive monsters and dragons.”

The site also claims that A24 is allowing potential international buyers to read Garland’s Elden Ring script, but only with a studio staff member present (for security reasons, naturally).

It was reported last week that the Elden Ring movie is the most expensive film A24 has ever produced – Deadline’s report today pegs it at “between $175 million-200 million, but closer to the latter” – and now comes word that the studio, which fully financed the film, is looking to mitigate some of that risk by bringing in a partner with very deep pockets: Amazon.

According to Deadline, Amazon MGM Studios has now acquired “a bunch of international pay-1 streaming rights... The pact is understood to cover a large number of international markets, and sources speculate to us that it is easily worth tens of millions of dollars. We hear the deal could also potentially lead to interesting activations on Amazon’s Twitch platform.”

The film’s huge price tag makes Elden Ring one of the most expensive films that will be shopped at next month’s American Film Market, which touts itself as “the premier marketplace for the acquisition, development, financing, and distribution of independent film, television, and premium content for audiences worldwide.”

Potential buyers at AFM will reportedly be treated to an Elden Ring movie presentation of some kind, including possibly seeing the very first footage from this highly-anticipated film.

After some set photos made their way online , Elden Ring wrapped filming in July and is scheduled to open in theaters on March 3, 2028.

In addition to Kit O’Connor, the cast includes Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Nick Offerman and Peter Serafinowicz .

Are you excited by the prospect of a three-hour Elden Ring movie? Let us know in the comments.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

items.title: 'Elden Ring' Will Be Biggest Movie At A Market, Amazon Joins A24 Film
items.summary: A24's Fantasy Epic 'Elden Ring' Heads To AFM As The Biggest Movie Ever On Sale At A Market; Amazon Joins Pic Starring Kit Connor.
items.content:
EXCLUSIVE : A24 ‘s fantasy video game adaptation Elden Ring is heading to the American Film Market, where it’ll be the biggest-budget stand-alone project ever on sale at a film or TV market.

We hear from sources the budget is being pegged between $175 million-$200 million but closer to the latter, which takes the project beyond previous tentpoles that have hit markets, including the latest Hunger Games installment. Mel Gibson’s upcoming Resurrection of the Christ came with a near-$200M price tag but across two films.

items.title: STARSCOURGE RADAHN JOINS THE ELDEN RING FIGUARTS MINI SERIES

items.content:
The roar of the Red Lion echoes to the heavens.

He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed him from a fate worse than death. Now, the power of this greatest of Carian generals can rest in the palm of your hand. Standing 12 cm (4.7 in) tall, Starscourge Radahn is stylized figure that features simple articulation, interchangeable left- and right-hand parts that hold his Starscourge Greatsword, his detachable scrawny steed, and a dedicated display stand. Produced with the super-deformed proportions of the FIGURARTS Mini series, Starscourge Radahn is molded from quality PVC and ABS with exact attention to detail paid even at this miniature size. His golden armor, his raging snarl, even the gravity crests on his blades can be made out with perfect clarity. Pre-orders for this charming miniature figure are available now on the Bandai Namco Store. Do not tary, every other limited edition in this series has sold out. *This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: Patch Notes Version 1.17
items.summary: Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING . This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC , scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026 , and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before
items.content:
Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

    [/*]

  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.

    [/*]

  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

    [/*]

The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows: Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Balance Adjustments

Changed certain items found in the field or obtained by defeating certain powerful enemies in the Realm of Shadow to higher-tier items or other treasures. Note: Items already that were already found will not be changed.

Weapons

  • Smithscript Dagger / Rellana's Twin Blades → Increased critical hit power.

    [/*]

  • Smithscript Axe / Smithscript Spear / Spear of the Impaler → Reduced the stamina consumption of weapon-throwing attacks. → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.

    [/*]

  • Carian Sorcery Sword → Changed Intelligence scaling so that it now increases the attack power of all damage types.

    [/*]

  • Smithscript Greathammer → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.

    [/*]

  • Golem Fist → Increased the range of the fist-launching heavy attack.

    [/*]

  • Firespark Perfume Bottle / Lightning Perfume Bottle / Chilling Perfume Bottle / Frenzyflame Perfume Bottle / Deadly Poison Perfume Bottle → Increased attack power.

    [/*]

  • Lordsworn's Shield / Briar Greatshield / Spiked Palisade Shield / Icon Shield / Golden Beast Crest Shield / Manor Towershield / Crossed-Tree Towershield / Inverted Hawk Towershield / Dragon Towershield / Distinguished Greatshield / Gilded Greatshield / Black Steel Greatshield / Ant's Skull Plate / Erdtree Greatshield → Increased guard boost. → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Wooden Greatshield / Cuckoo Greatshield / Redmane Greatshield / Golden Greatshield / Crucible Hornshield / Dragonclaw Shield / Eclipse Crest Greatshield / Jellyfish Shield / One-Eyed Shield → Increased guard boost.

    [/*]

  • Haligtree Crest Greatshield → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased the time before an attack can be performed with a right-hand weapon immediately after attacking with this weapon equipped in the left hand.

    [/*]

Skills

  • Parry → Improved parry performance. → Reduced the time before various actions can be performed after activation when used with Daggers, Curved Swords, or Small Shields.

    [/*]

  • Storm Wall → Changed the skill so that it no longer consumes FP when used. → Improved parry performance.

    [/*]

  • Thops's Barrier → Improved parry performance.

    [/*]

Sorceries

  • Founding Rain of Stars → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • Carian Retaliation → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • Meteorite → Reduced casting time.

    [/*]

  • Meteorite of Astel → Reduced casting time.

    [/*]

  • Gravitational Missile → Changed the spell so that the gravity projectile does not explode immediately upon striking terrain such as the ground or a wall.

    [/*]

Incantations

  • Feather of the Divine Bird → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • O, Flame! → Expanded attack range.

    [/*]

  • Rain of Fire → Increased power.

    [/*]

PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments

Weapons

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased damage taken from attacks by other players while attacking.

    [/*]

Incantations

  • Rugalea's Roar → Reduced power against other players.

    [/*]

  • Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay → Reduced the amount of time other player characters are unable to move from hit reactions when struck by these incantations.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where critical hits dealt with Great Katana weapon types had lower-than-expected power against large enemies. Fixed a bug where jumping attacks with Great Katana weapon types could be parried.

PC-Only Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug that prevented camera control with the mouse during NPC dialogue when using keyboard and mouse controls Fixed a bug in the "Keyboard/Mouse Settings" section of the system menu in which selecting the reset option did not restore various settings to their defaults The version number shown in the lower-right corner of the title screen after applying this update will be as follows:

App Ver. 1.17 Regulation Ver. 1.17

This update is required for online play.

We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy ELDEN RING more comfortably. Thank you for your continued support.
